subject: general
question: Which Chinese traveler mentions a Maitraka ruler named Shiladitya?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Hiuen Tsang**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hiuen Tsang**, also known as Xuanzang, was a **Chinese Buddhist monk, scholar, and traveler** who visited India during the reign of King Harsha in the 7th century CE.
 
• During his travels, Hiuen Tsang extensively documented the **political, social, and religious conditions of India**.
 
• He mentioned a **Maitraka ruler named Shiladitya**, who was the ruler of **Vallabhi** (modern-day Gujarat).
 
• Shiladitya was renowned for his **administrative skills and patronage of Buddhism**, which Hiuen Tsang appreciated and documented.
 
• The Maitraka dynasty ruled from around the **6th to 8th century CE**, with Vallabhi as its capital.
 
• Hiuen Tsang's records are considered a **valuable source of Indian history**, providing insights into the culture, education, and governance of the time.
 
• His writings include details about major Indian cities, universities like **Nalanda**, and interactions with kings and scholars during his journey.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **I-Tsing**__

 __
 
• **I-Tsing** was a **Chinese Buddhist pilgrim** who traveled to India in the **7th century CE**.
 
• He is known for documenting his experiences in a work called the **"Record of Buddhist Practices Sent Home from the Southern Sea."**
 
• I-Tsing focused more on religious practices and the study of **Buddhism**, but he did not mention Shiladitya.
 
 
 
• **Fa-Hien**__
 __
 
• **Fa-Hien** was a **Chinese Buddhist monk and traveler** who visited India in the **5th century CE**.
 
• His accounts primarily document the **Gupta Empire** and its religious practices, but there is no mention of the Maitraka ruler Shiladitya.
 
 
 
• **Faxian**__
 
 
• **Faxian** is another name for Fa-Hien, and his travel accounts are the same as those attributed to Fa-Hien.
